page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, configured with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a low memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1D cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a distinct performance profile. The AMD EPYC processor delivers strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% during stress-ng testing. However, multi-core CPU scaling is relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% for both stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the PassMark memory score and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression are poor, ranking in the bottom 10% of tested systems. Uncached large-block memory read and write speeds maintain average performance at 43.63 GB/sec and 30.48 GB/sec respectively, while small-block cached reads are weak at 253.45 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the n2d-highcpu-4 is its highly constrained memory capacity of 4.0 GB, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications or large-scale database operations. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a dedicated AMD EPYC hardware profile optimized for compute-heavy tasks that do not require substantial memory overhead. It is best suited for single-threaded processing tasks, basic web serving, lightweight text processing, and small-scale language model text generation using compact models.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 4.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. With 2 physical cores and a 1.0 GB memory-per-core ratio, this instance is designed for compute-focused workloads with low memory requirements. Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 25%, though multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth remain weak. The instance lacks bundled local storage, GPU accelerators, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Due to its constrained memory capacity and poor multi-threaded decompression performance, the n2d-highcpu-4 is best suited for single-threaded processing, basic web serving, and lightweight text processing tasks rather than memory-intensive database operations.
